Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the Q&A are to press star then one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY24 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; Casey Wong, Chief Product Officer; Riley Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and Pat Nguyen, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY24. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our Pipeline Optimizer and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: MRR trends, Gross margin, Next quarter ARR guidance, NRR performance, Product roadmap, Free cash flow, Operating expense breakdown, and Churn analysis.

Let me start with a highlight on our product roadmap, which has been central to our success. At CloudForge, our mission is clear: to empower mid-market and enterprise teams with an AI-native DevOps platform that streamlines CI/CD pipelines and accelerates deployments at scale. We've powered over 5,000 enterprise customers globally, with our customer base expanding 28% year-over-year.

Q2 highlights included the continued rollout of our CloudForge AI Copilot, our generative AI assistant that launched in beta last quarter. Adoption has reached 68% among top customers, up from 42% initially, contributing to a 22% NRR uplift as teams use it for predictive pipeline tuning and automated optimizations. One manufacturing client reduced deployment cycles by 35%, akin to gains seen with tools like GitHub Copilot in dev workflows.

We also delivered the Unified Data Fabric, integrating seamlessly with Snowflake and Databricks for zero-ETL from 150+ sources, cutting time-to-insight by 40% and boosting premium analytics attach rates from 32% to 47%. This has unlocked $120 million in ARR pipeline. Additionally, our Zero-Trust Security Suite, with adaptive MFA and ML anomaly detection, addressed rising threats—up 19% year-over-year per industry reports—driving a 25% reduction in security-related churn risks and 18% seat growth in regulated sectors.

Regionally, North America at 62% of ARR saw 75% Copilot adoption and 125% net expansion. EMEA grew customers 35% year-over-year with GDPR-ready Data Fabric features. APAC surged 52%, aided by our Tokyo data center slashing latency 60%.

For the back half of 2024, we're pushing our AI-first agenda:

First, Copilot Pro Enterprise Edition launches in Q3, enabling autonomous pipeline orchestration across Slack, Teams, and Zoom integrations. Betas with 50 enterprises hit 92% satisfaction and 28% faster resolutions, priced at $50 per user monthly, targeting a $2.5 billion TAM with $350 million pipeline.

Second, our Marketplace beta in Q4 offers 200+ low-code integrations with AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, embracing composable DevOps. Gartner forecasts 40% of SaaS composable by 2026; partners like AWS and Snowflake project $200 million co-sell ARR by FY25, cutting CAC 22%.

Third, vertical accelerators: Healthcare with Kubernetes-HIPAA compliance goes GA soon, speeding onboarding 45%; retail edge-compute for real-time monitoring eyes 32% CLV lifts.

We're allocating 18% of R&D—$145 million annually—to frontier models with Anthropic and OpenAI partners, hitting 85% on-time delivery. AI ARR cohort, now 22%, should grow 30-35% year-over-year, with NPS at 68.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $34 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $650 million to $670 million.

Let's dive deeper into our key metrics, starting with MRR trends, which serve as the North Star for our business here at CloudForge, our cloud-native DevOps platform powering CI/CD pipelines for over 5,000 enterprise customers globally. In Q2 FY24, we delivered total MRR of $58.2 million, up 15% quarter-over-quarter and 42% year-over-year. This is our 11th straight quarter of at least 15% QoQ growth, surpassing the SaaS industry average of 10-12% from Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud Index.

Net new MRR additions totaled $8.1 million, broken down as follows: New Logo MRR at $3.4 million, up 20% QoQ from 12 net new enterprise deals averaging $285K ACV, including a Fortune 100 financial services migration from on-prem Jenkins to our Kubernetes-orchestrated pipelines and a healthcare provider like Teladoc for HIPAA DevSecOps. Sales velocity rose 18% via refined targeting of 50+ engineer teams scaling microservices.

Expansion MRR led with $4.2 million, 52% of adds, as NRR stayed at 118% above our 115% target. Upsells to AI-powered Pipeline Optimizer—auto-tuning builds up to 40% like GitHub Copilot—and Observability Suite integrating with Datadog and New Relic shone, with top 20 customers expanding 35% on average, including a hyperscaler across 15 teams.

Churn and contraction offset was minimal at negative $0.5 million, with gross revenue churn at 4.2% annualized, below 7-10% benchmarks. Multi-year renewals had 8% escalators, though SMB saw slight contraction from macro IT budget caution.

Notably, expansion accelerated 25% QoQ from $3.4 million in Q1, thanks to Pipeline Optimizer launch, mirroring CircleCI's orb expansions with 2.5x faster deployments. New logos slowed 5% in EMEA from GDPR delays but Americas offset it.

Regionally: Americas (72% of MRR) at $41.9 million, +17% QoQ/+45% YoY, strong in fintech and AI/ML; EMEA (18%) $10.5 million, +12%/+38%, via AWS partnerships despite Brexit FX; APAC (10%) $5.8 million, +14%/+35%, Tokyo DC unlocking SoftBank deals vs. Harness.

These trends affirm platform consolidation reducing Jenkins/GitLab tool sprawl, with zero-trust and serverless investments for 120%+ NRR. Q3 net new MRR guides to $8.5-$9.0 million, 14-16% QoQ growth, upside from AI Agent beta automating 70% YAML configs.

Moving to gross margin performance, which highlights our asset-light SaaS leverage. GAAP gross margin hit 82.5%, up 130 bps from Q1's 81.2% and 360 bps from Q2 2023's 78.9%. Non-GAAP was 84.1%, 11th straight sequential gain, excluding $4.2 million in SBC and intangibles.

YoY improvement overcame Q2 2023's $12 million hosting ramp for AI workflows—excess AWS GPUs for GenAI inflating COGS 8%. Now optimized.

Sequentially: Infrastructure efficiencies drove 80 bps, COGS $56.7 million or 17.5% of revenue vs. 18.8% Q1. Hosting (65% COGS) cut via multi-cloud—25% to Google TPUs/Azure, discounts, AutoScale AI dropping per-user costs 14%. ARPU steady at $142 for 1.2 million DAUs.

Product mix added 40 bps: Enterprise subs (88% margins) up 32% YoY to $285 million, 72% of ARR from 65%. NRR 118% aids, with 45% attach for Analytics and AI Co-Pilot.

Support efficiencies: Headcount to 0.8% revenue via AI chatbot resolving 62% Tier 1 tickets like ServiceNow's agent. Cap software amortization $8.1 million offset by revenue.

Regionally: NA (58% revenue) 83.8%; EMEA 82.1% up 200 bps via Dublin DC; APAC 80.4% despite FX.

Like Snowflake or Adobe, we target 84% non-GAAP FY-end via AI ops. Q3 may see $5-7 million GPU refresh, recouped 2025 at 85% utilization. Gross profit up 28% YoY to $323 million, 42% adjusted FCF margins.

Next, our NRR performance, a pillar of our land-and-expand. Q2 NRR was 118%, sixth quarter above 115%, up 300 bps YoY from 115%, outperforming SaaS averages of 105-110% and peers like Snowflake at 120%+.

Expansion contributed 28%, up from Q1's 24%: 15% new seats from viral hybrid team adoption, 12% premium upsells, 1% geo expansions. ForgeAI engine (35% attach like Adobe Firefly) averaged $45K ARR per upsell, up 20% QoQ; AWS Bedrock integrations cross-sold to 40% AWS accounts. Enterprise (65% ARR) drove 70%, Q4 FY23 cohorts at 32% annualized.

Contraction at 6%, flat QoQ, managed via 'right-size' converting 25% risks to expansions. Top whales zero contraction.

Churn 4%, down 100 bps YoY, logo sub-2% vs. 5-7% benchmarks. NPS 58 up from 52; SMB (<$10K) sensitive but down to 6%; enterprise 1.2% with 90% multi-year.

Regions: US 122%, EMEA 116% DACH strong, APAC 108% improving with Tokyo residency. Mid-market 114%, enterprise 125%.

Ahead, 115%+ via usage pricing pilots (+5-7% expansions), renewal automation, vertical playbooks.

On free cash flow, another strength. Q2 FCF was $45.2 million, +28% YoY, 142% of adjusted EBITDA. TTM margin 32% from 25%; FY guide $195-205 million, 25-30% growth, 31-33% margins.

Subscription revenue $652 million, +32% YoY, DBNER 118%. Expansions 42% new ARR.

Ops cash $48.7 million, 107% revenue; DSO 52 from 58 via 68% annual/multi-year bookings.

CapEx $3.5 million (1% revenue), AWS Graviton savings. Rule of 40 score 60.

Regions: NA $32.5 million (72%), EMEA $8.1 million +45%, APAC $4.6 million +60%.

FCF funds M&A in verticals, $100 million buyback at <22x EV/FCF. AI boosts NRR 25%, churn 4.8%; target 35%+ margins FY26.

Operating expenses totaled $118 million non-GAAP, 78% revenue, down 200 bps YoY, on track for Rule 40 of 45+ (28% growth, 22% margin).

R&D $42 million, +35% YoY, 28% revenue: +120 engineers on AI (ForgeAI like Copilot/Firefly, $8 million compute), cyber ($6 million zero-trust), scalability. Flat QoQ; 45% EMEA spend (Dublin AI Act). FY 27-29%.

Sales & Marketing $52 million, +22% YoY, 34% revenue: +15% to 450 heads, CAC payback 16 months from inbound/product-led. ABM/SEO 25% logos, partners 18% ARR. APAC +50%; seq -5%. LTV:CAC 4.2x; FY 32-34%, payback to 14 months.

G&A $24 million, flat YoY, 16% revenue: Automation leverage; people +5%, fees flat (-20% AI legal), facilities -10%. ForgeOps cuts cycles 50%. FY 15%, to 13% FY25.

Now, churn analysis. Logo churn 4.2%, down 80 bps QoQ below 5.5% historical; revenue churn 3.8%, driving 118% NRR. Q2 FY23 cohort GDR 92%, +300 bps.

Voluntary churn up to 3.1%: Macro (22%, $45K ARR, fin serv +150 bps like ADP); integration (18%, legacy stacks, onboarding NPS 72); competition (12%, HubSpot/Pipedrive/SF); value (15%). NA 3.5%, EMEA 5.1% GDPR/FX, APAC 6.2% localization.

Mitigations: ForgeGuard ML (87% precision, recovered $2.3 million); CS +25% to 180, SuccessTracks (78% activation); Q2 APIs/zero-ETL (+60% setup speed), Copilot beta (+25% adoption); Growth Bands (30% budget churn stemmed); EMEA VARs, APAC localization. LTV:CAC to 5x FY25; recession NRR 110%. Top-quartile vs. Bessemer.

Finally, Q3 ARR guidance: Ended Q2 at $1.25 billion, +22% YoY/+6% QoQ. Guide Q3 $1.32-$1.34 billion, 5-7% seq/24-26% YoY; FY $5.4 billion +23%.

New logos 35% adds ($45-50 million, 250 customers, $500K+ ACV Fortune 100 betas for AI Agent like ServiceNow Now Assist). Expansions 65%, NRR 115-120%, RPO 2.2x.

Nexlify Horizon multimodal LLMs, Snowflake partners, 70% pilots. Regions: Americas 7%, EMEA 6%, APAC 8%. Pipeline $4.2 billion +30% YoY. Risks FX/churn/cycles, but 70% margins, Rule 40 25.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Casey Wong will provide update on product roadmap.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of Pipeline Optimizer Pro. This new feature significantly improves deployment speeds and cost efficiencies. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Casey. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 30% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Pat Nguyen:
Thank you, Riley. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 15% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of Pipeline Optimizer on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. The Pipeline Optimizer has been transformative for growth, contributing over 25% of our Q2 expansions and accelerating overall revenue by embedding AI directly into core workflows. Attach rates are hitting 45% among eligible customers, well above our 30% internal target. This exceeded expectations by 50% in terms of adoption velocity, as early betas showed outsized build time reductions. Competitively, we're up against Harness and CircleCI, but our ML-driven auto-optimization and seamless Kubernetes integration set us apart. Differentiation comes via our unified platform reducing tool sprawl, plus native multi-cloud support and zero-trust security that incumbents are still playing catch-up on.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Chris Lee:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Chris. International expansion is a priority, with APAC as a high-conviction bet. Plans include doubling our Tokyo and Singapore data centers by year-end and localizing for kanji/script support. Key targets are Japan (keiretsu firms via SoftBank ties), Australia/ANZ fintech, and India hyperscalers. We expect 3x ROI within two years on $50 million invested, based on current 35% YoY APAC MRR growth. Challenges include regulatory hurdles like data sovereignty, currency volatility—we hedge 80%—and localization, but partnerships and edge nodes are mitigating these effectively.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Kim with JPMorgan.

Dana Kim:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Dana. Churn management leverages proactive AI like ForgeGuard, flagging risks early and recovering ARR through CS interventions. NRR trended up to 118% this quarter, steady from expansions offsetting minor macro drags. Retention strategies include tiered CS playbooks, automated onboarding boosting activation 78%, and feature releases like zero-ETL cutting friction. Pricing via Growth Bands stemmed 30% of budget churn without uplift. Long-term, we're targeting 125% NRR by FY26, matching leaders via AI moats and verticals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Evan Patel with Barclays.

Evan Patel:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Jordan Lee:
Sure, Evan. CAC averaged $45,000 this quarter, down 10% year-over-year from efficient inbound and partner channels contributing 18% of ARR. Payback periods improved to 16 months overall, 12 months for enterprises, thanks to higher ACVs and faster ramps with AI demos shortening cycles.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
